content.value_statement: Unchecked exceptions hide failure paths in TypeScript and make async workflows hard to reason about. This skill shows practical fp-ts Either and TaskEither patterns for explicit, composable error handling.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to replace throw and try catch with Either values.
Shows how to chain failing TypeScript operations with Either and chainW.
Demonstrates validation error accumulation with NonEmptyArray and sequenceS.
Shows TaskEither patterns for async fetch, database, retry, and fallback workflows.
Covers partial success reporting for lists and bulk operations.
Provides a quick reference for common Either and TaskEither operations.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not install fp-ts or modify projects by itself.
Examples may need updates for local fp-ts versions and project conventions.
It does not run tests or prove that a refactor preserves behavior.
Real API and database code still needs project-specific security review.

use_cases.title: Refactor Exception-Heavy Services
use_cases.description: Convert throwing service functions into typed Either returns that callers must handle explicitly.

use_cases.title: Design Async Failure Pipelines
use_cases.description: Model fetch, database, retry, and fallback flows with TaskEither instead of nested try catch blocks.

use_cases.title: Collect Form Validation Errors
use_cases.description: Accumulate field-level validation errors so users can fix all input issues at once.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Either Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how Either represents success and failure in TypeScript. Use a small user lookup example and avoid advanced terminology.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Throwing Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this TypeScript function to return Either instead of throwing exceptions. Explain each error case and how callers handle Left and Right.

prompt_templates.title: Build a TaskEither Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Composing async operations that can fail
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this async workflow into a TaskEither pipeline. Include typed errors, chaining, fallback behavior, and the final fold point.

prompt_templates.title: Design Validation Accumulation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an fp-ts validation approach that returns all errors, not only the first one. Include field-level errors and caller handling guidance.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to replace scattered try catch blocks in an order workflow.
output_examples.output: The response identifies each failure boundary, proposes typed error values, and describes a clean Either pipeline with final handling.

output_examples.input: A backend engineer needs safer async fetch and database error handling.
output_examples.output: The response recommends TaskEither wrappers, typed network and database errors, retry or fallback placement, and a single final fold.

output_examples.input: A frontend engineer wants form validation to show every invalid field at once.
output_examples.output: The response describes accumulating NonEmptyArray field errors and mapping them to user-facing messages.

best_practices: Use explicit error types that describe expected failures clearly.
Wrap throwing, nullable, and promise-based APIs at system boundaries.
Handle Either and TaskEither results at the final caller boundary.
anti_patterns: Do not mix unchecked throws inside functions that claim to return Either.
Do not erase specific error types into vague strings too early.
Do not execute TaskEither pipelines before composition is complete.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps TypeScript developers represent expected failures as values with fp-ts Either and TaskEither.

faq.question: Does it require prior functional programming experience?
faq.answer: No. The skill explains practical patterns with examples and avoids heavy theory.

faq.question: Can it help with async code?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers TaskEither for promises, fetch calls, database calls, retries, and fallbacks.

faq.question: Can it collect multiple validation errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows validation applicative patterns for collecting all form or input errors.

faq.question: Does it change my project automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance that an agent or developer can apply in context.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
